subject: cs201
question: Explain why a hash table lookup is O(1) on average but O(n) in the worst case.
student_answer:
Average case is O(1) because a good hash function spreads keys evenly so each bucket
has very few entries. Worst case is O(n) because if many keys hash to the same bucket, 
you end up having to scan through all of them one by one, which is linear.
student_feedback: Great job! You clearly explained both why the average case is O(1) through even distribution and why the worst case is O(n) due to collisions and linear scanning.
instructor_feedback: The student successfully met both criteria. They explicitly mentioned that a good hash function spreads keys evenly resulting in O(1) average time (c1), and described hash collisions leading to a linear scan of all items in the bucket for O(n) worst-case time (c2).

question: What is the law of conservation of mass and why does it hold true in a chemical reaction?

same total afterward — nothing just vanishes or appears out of nowhere. That's because
a reaction doesn't destroy or make new atoms, it just shuffles the existing ones around
into different combinations.
student_feedback: Great job! You clearly explained both the definition of the law of conservation of mass and the atomic reasoning behind why it holds true.
instructor_feedback: The student successfully stated that mass is neither created nor destroyed (phrased as 'nothing just vanishes or appears out of nowhere') satisfying criterion c1. They also correctly explained that the law holds true because atoms are not created or destroyed, but merely rearranged ('shuffles the existing ones around into different combinations'), satisfying criterion c2.

question: Explain the concept of opportunity cost.
student_answer:
It's basically what you're giving up by picking one thing over another. If you had 
several options and chose one, opportunity cost is the benefit of whichever other 
option would have been your best choice instead.
student_feedback: Great job! You clearly explained opportunity cost by identifying it as the benefit of the best alternative given up.
instructor_feedback: The student accurately captured both components of the required definition: sacrificing an option to choose another, and specifically identifying that the sacrificed value corresponds to the 'next best' alternative.

subject: physics101
question: State Newton's second law and use it to find the acceleration of a 4 kg object when a net force of 20 N acts on it.
student_answer: Newton's first law says an object keeps its state of motion unless a force acts on it, and the third law says every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The second law, which is the one that matters here, says the net force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration, F = ma. Rearranging gives a = F / m, so with F = 20 N and m = 4 kg the acceleration is 20 / 4 = 5 m/s², in the direction of the net force. This is also why a heavier object accelerates less under the same force.
student_feedback: Great job! You stated Newton's second law correctly and accurately calculated the acceleration with the right units.
instructor_feedback: The student correctly stated Newton's second law (F = ma) fulfilling criterion c1 completely. They also correctly calculated the acceleration as 5 m/s² and included the units, fulfilling criterion c2 despite adding extra discussion about the first and third laws.
